title: Everyone Who Calls on the Name of the Lord
summary: Christianity is the great equalizer. The only ones God rejects are those who reject him. Whoever you are, call on his name.
exhortation: Christianity is the greatest equalizer. There is no race, tribe, language, gender or background that God has not called to repent and be saved. The only ones God rejects are those who reject him.

Are you weighed down by a sin you think is too great? Don't believe the lie. God will not reject you if you come to him in repentance. Is your background as far from Christianity as it could possibly be? It isn't far enough that God can't save you. Did you grow up Christian and wander far from God? Even so, his grace is available to you now.

As sinful human beings, we like to separate ourselves by our differences: culture, language, skin color, country. But God doesn't look at outward appearances. He looks at the heart. He isn't looking for a certain personality type. He's looking for someone who will humble himself and repent, and that person he will never refuse.

Listen to Revelation 7:9-10: "After this I looked, and behold, a great multitude that no one could number, from every nation, from all tribes and peoples and languages, standing before the throne and before the Lamb, clothed in white robes, with palm branches in their hands, and crying out with a loud voice, 'Salvation belongs to our God who sits on the throne, and to the Lamb!'" What a glorious picture of God's grace and mercy, saving people from all over the world, from every kind of sin, in every generation.
prayer: Lord, how can we not speak? How can we not tell of the great work you have done, that you are mighty to save? A thousand times we failed, and you brought us back, for a gathering of people who will proclaim your name for all eternity. This is the work you are about. This is the work of the kingdom and the work your Spirit is doing, and we simply get to join in it. May we join in this great and mighty work.

For anyone listening who is struggling with depression and asking, "What is my life for?", for anyone stuck in a mundane, day-after-day existence that doesn't feel meaningful: this is meaningful. A life fully committed to your kingdom, not the endless distractions we fill our lives with, is a life of purpose, full of joy. Fill our lives again. Fill us with your Spirit so that we do your will and your purposes. In Jesus' name.
